name: Yogurt
works_with: macOS 14.4+ on Apple Silicon, Windows 10 2004+ (x64), Ubuntu 22.04+ or similar (x64)
short: A free desktop app that records your calls, transcribes them and writes meeting notes, with the AI running on your own computer.
what: Yogurt is an open source meeting notes app. It records your microphone and call audio without adding a bot to the meeting, writes a live transcript and then a summary. Transcription uses whisper.cpp and the summaries come from a local open-weight model through llama.cpp. You can search past meetings, ask questions with links to the source, and export notes as Markdown.
who: Anyone who wants AI meeting notes but would rather keep the audio and transcripts on their own machine. Skip it if your computer has less than 8 GB of memory, or if you need speaker names or calendar links on Windows or Linux, since those are Mac only for now.
needs: A Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14.4 or newer, a 64-bit PC with Windows 10 (version 2004) or newer, or 64-bit Linux with Ubuntu 22.04 or newer
Room for the models: about 5 GB first, and the best model for your machine can be 14 GB or more

steps.title: Download the app
steps.text: The README links a build for each system on the latest release: `Yogurt-mac-arm64.dmg`, `Yogurt-windows-x64.exe` or `Yogurt-linux-x86_64.AppImage`. Get it from https://github.com/FrigadeHQ/yogurt/releases/latest.

steps.title: Get past the Windows warning
steps.text: If Windows says "Windows protected your PC", click More info, then Run anyway. The app is not signed with a Microsoft certificate yet.

steps.title: Let setup download the models
steps.text: Yogurt downloads a smaller notes model first, then the best one your computer can run well. If your computer is too slow, setup tells you. Recording works once setup finishes.

steps.title: Record a call
steps.text: Start recording your microphone and call audio and add your own notes if you like. Yogurt offers to record when a Zoom, Teams or Meet call starts, and stops when the call ends.

steps.title: Optional: connect an assistant app
steps.text: In Settings, AI apps, turn on access, copy the helper command and add it as a local MCP server in your assistant app. Access is off by default.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Record one call, then ask a question across your meetings and follow the link to the source in the transcript.

watch: No bot joins the call, so tell the other people on the call that you are recording.
Meeting data stays on your computer, but Yogurt goes online for model downloads and update checks.
With MCP access on, any app running under your user account can read your meetings, notes and transcripts, and an assistant app may send what it reads to its own online model.
Speaker names need Accessibility permission on Mac and are Mac only, as is calendar access.
The Windows build is not signed yet.
